A3_S7_D1: ^Narrator: The flipping of a tome that contains your family tree. Small hands that belonged to you point at a missing name.
^Narrator: Her voice clips, shutting the book and opening another, redirecting you to a fresh page.
A3_S7_D2: ^Young Noelle: How did you and Mother meet?
^Father: Oh… your mother was always the brightest on our island.
^Father: She had dreams and ideals for how we could build a better life. Especially as the floods will happen when we’d become adults…
^Father: I suppose she felt like she had a duty to protect us.
^Father: Haha, I wasn’t as clever compared to her! But your grandad was very happy to have a daughter-in-law who’d lead the island with pride.
^Young Noelle: But you were the one who was a Tempest!
^Narrator: Your father smiles, picking up your small frame to sit atop his lap, and taps the space on your heart.
^Father: ‘Tempest’ may have been my family name, but it belongs to anyone who’s willing to brave the storm.
^Father: …Or, become it, in order to lead us to brighter days.
^Young Noelle: Now that Mother is chief, are you disappointed?
^Father: Oh, why would I be disappointed?
^Father: Your mother had always wanted the chance to make a difference. And now, I can do what I love.
^Father: Caring for you… and researching in my office to my heart’s content!
^Father: Now come. We still have time before your classes to forage on the beach.
^Father: Let’s see what treasures we might find.
A3_S7_D3: ^Narrator: …The outside world was completely different from what your mother had told you.
^Narrator: Creatures are indeed capable of speech — but are just as empathetic and kind as any human. Not mindless monsters.
^Narrator: Everyone here is able to live in coexistence.
^Narrator: …If so, what about the Great Disaster?
^Narrator: Was Noah’s story all that meets the eye?
